hook.title: File routes, SSR, SSG and ISR. On components that run once.
hook.lede: `@pyreon/zero` lets every route pick its render mode with a one-line export or a glob rule, and deploys to Node, Bun, Deno, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare or static hosting. Under it is Pyreon: a page component runs once, and only the nodes that read a changed signal update.

proof.label: render modes, chosen per route: `ssr`, `ssg`, `isr`, `spa`, by a route export or a `routeRules` glob
proof.source: docs/src/content/docs/zero.md (Route Module Exports; Per-route render modes)

proof.label: deploy adapters: node, bun, deno, static, vercel, cloudflare, netlify, auto-detected on the three hosted platforms
on one harness and the same app, Zero and Next.js 16 App Router among them: SSR throughput, TTFB, first-load JS, hydration. No result is published yet, so we claim none.

table.title: Zero and Next.js, line by line.
table.note: Next.js is a meta-framework, so it is compared with `@pyreon/zero`, Pyreon's. There is no published head-to-head between the two yet; this table compares what each one does. For framework numbers (Pyreon against the React that Next runs on), see /compare/react.

rows.pyreon: `export const renderMode = 'ssr' | 'ssg' | 'isr' | 'spa'`, `routeRules` globs, and `mode: 'auto'` (experimental), which infers each route's mode and prints the result at build.
rows.rival: Static, dynamic and ISR per route through route segment config and the data APIs a page uses.

rows.pyreon: A `.server.ts` sibling exports `serverLoader`; it never enters the client bundle, and a client navigation fetches the whole route chain in one request.
rows.rival: React Server Components and server functions.

rows.pyreon: A route's `action` export with `defineAction`, submitted by `<Form>` and read with `useSubmission`.
Seven adapters; on Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare builds the adapter is picked from the environment.
rows.rival: `next start` on Node, static export, and first-class on Vercel; other hosts through their own integrations.

rows.pyreon: Pyreon: components run once, signals update single nodes.
rows.rival: React: components re-render; memoisation controls the cost.

rows.pyreon: Not compared yet. `examples/stacks-bench` measures Zero, Next.js 16 App Router and seven other stacks on the same app; run it yourself.

rows.topic: Native apps from the same components
rows.pyreon: PMTC compiles the same `.tsx` to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose (experimental).
rows.rival: Web only; a React Native app is a separate codebase.
Years in production, a large plugin and hosting ecosystem, and Vercel behind it.

code.title: One server-rendered page, cached and revalidated.
code.caption: A user page that loads on the server and is cached with stale-while-revalidate. Next.js does it in a server component; Zero splits the server-only loader into a sibling file that the client bundle never imports.

rival.label: Next.js App Router

pyreon.label: Pyreon Zero

code.checked: Zero side: the page and an equivalent loader typecheck against the repo; `serverLoader`, `renderMode = 'isr'` (60 s default) and `useLoaderData<T>()` are as documented in zero.md and `packages/core/router/src/loader.ts`. Next side: App Router conventions (`params` is a Promise since Next 15); not compiled here.

items.instead: Nothing: pages are Pyreon components and run once.
There are no server components to fence off. Server-only code lives in a `.server.ts` file that the client bundle never imports.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick Next.js
items: You want React Server Components and the React library catalog behind them.
You deploy on Vercel and use its platform features end to end.
Your team ships Next.js today and re-rendering is not what slows the app down.
You need a meta-framework with years of production use behind it.

migrate.title: A Next.js app is a React app.
migrate.text: Start with `@pyreon/react-compat` to run your components on Pyreon, then move routes into Zero's file router (`src/routes`).
